content: Health science is an applied field of science that focuses on health and encompasses numerous sub-disciplines. It involves two primary approaches: the study and research of the human body and health-related issues to understand how humans and animals function, and the application of this knowledge to enhance health, prevent diseases, and develop cures. Health research is grounded in the fundamental sciences of biology, chemistry, and physics, as well as various interdisciplinary fields such as medical sociology. Key research-oriented fields that significantly contribute to health science include biochemistry, epidemiology, and genetics. Applied health sciences aim not only to understand health better but also to directly improve the health of individuals and populations. Examples of applied health sciences include biomedical engineering, biotechnology, nursing, nutrition, pharmacology, pharmacy, public health, psychology, physical therapy, and medicine. The delivery of services to enhance people's health is referred to as healthcare. According to the World Health Organization, healthcare encompasses all goods and services designed to promote health, including preventive, curative, and palliative interventions, whether directed at individuals or populations. Organized healthcare services may form a healthcare system, which can include government organizations like the National Health Service in the UK or collaborative efforts such as shared care between healthcare and social services. Medical research, both basic and applied, is conducted to improve the evaluation of new treatments for safety and efficacy through clinical trials or to develop new treatments in preclinical research. Advances in medical research have significantly contributed to increased human longevity over the past century. Major medical breakthroughs include vaccines for measles and polio, insulin for diabetes, antibiotics for various infections, medications for high blood pressure, improved treatments for AIDS, statins for atherosclerosis, microsurgical techniques, and increasingly effective cancer therapies. The Human Genome Project is expected to yield new diagnostic and therapeutic advancements. However, challenges such as antibiotic resistance and the obesity epidemic remain. Healthcare involves the prevention, treatment, and management of illnesses, as well as the preservation of mental and physical well-being through services provided by medical, nursing, and allied health professionals. Healthcare includes a wide range of traditional practices, such as dietetics, physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and respiratory therapy. It also encompasses the study and application of methods to prevent and cure diseases and disorders. Medical doctors, including physicians and surgeons, specialize in various branches of medicine, while other healthcare professionals focus on specific populations or care settings. Public health examines the impact of environmental factors, such as healthcare resource availability, on population health, often targeting specific groups like mothers and children. Dietitians educate individuals on proper nutrition, addressing specific dietary needs for populations such as diabetics, breastfeeding women, and those with celiac disease. Other areas of healthcare include first aid, triage, dental health, counseling, hospice care, home care, medical social work, alternative medicine, pharmacology, and toxicology. Veterinary medicine is dedicated to the care of animals, including disease prevention, treatment, and inspection of animal-derived food products. Health practices can be categorized into conventional Western practices, complementary and alternative medicine, spiritually-based healing, traditional medicine, and historical health practices. Conventional Western practices include allopathic medicine, dentistry, nursing, pharmacology, physical therapy, psychology, public health, and surgery. Complementary and alternative medicine encompasses practices like chiropractic, herbalism, homeopathy, naturopathy, and osteopathy (outside the USA). Spiritually-based healing includes methods such as Reiki, shamanism, and faith healing. Traditional medicine includes systems like Ayurveda, traditional Chinese medicine, and traditional Korean medicine. Historical health practices of interest include bloodletting, trepanation, and medieval medicine. Health science frequently intersects with medical ethics, addressing issues such as patient privacy, euthanasia, abortion, human cloning, stem cell research, and genetic engineering. These topics are often controversial and require careful ethical consideration. The origins of health science date back to the earliest human civilizations, as humans have always sought solutions for illness, injury, and health-related challenges like childbirth. Modern technology and advancements in pure sciences have significantly improved the scientific accuracy of health sciences. However, many cultures continue to use traditional remedies, including herbs and culturally specific practices, some of which lack scientific validation.
